Issue #2922 -- "value-to-declare pass not handling pointer case under -O1"

WHAT TO LOOK FOR, and what this link can and cannot show.

This is the PixTest::PixStructAnnotation_FloatN shader, compiled the way PixTest.cpp
compiles it (as_6_5, /Zi /Qembed_debug, -HV 2018, -enable-16bit-types).

Pane 1  DXC 1.6.2112, -O1   (last release that still had the bug)
Pane 2  DXC trunk,    -O1   (fixed)
Pane 3  DXC trunk,    -Od   (the configuration PixTest used to avoid the bug)

Look at the llvm.dbg record for the local variable "p" near the end of @main:

  Pane 3, -Od:        llvm.dbg.declare(metadata %struct.smallPayload.0* %p1, ...)
  Panes 1 and 2, -O1: llvm.dbg.value  (metadata %struct.smallPayload.0* %p1, ...)
                                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ POINTER operand

That pointer-typed dbg.value is the input DxilDbgValueToDbgDeclare::handleDbgValue used to
early-return on, dropping the variable, which is what made PixTest fail at -O1.

PANES 1 AND 2 AGREE, AND THAT IS THE POINT. (Their metadata node numbers differ; the
instruction and its operand types are the same.) The fix -- c0676c7ca, PR #4375, Apr 2022 --
is inside lib/DxilPIXPasses/, a pass reachable only through IDxcOptimizer. dxc.exe does not
run it, and Compiler Explorer cannot run it, so NO Compiler Explorer link can show this bug
being present or absent. This link shows only the precondition: that -O1 really does hand the
pass a pointer, on both sides of the fix.

The symptom itself was measured out-of-band by running each release's own
-dxil-dbg-value-to-dbg-declare through dxopt -external; see measure.py and
manual-case-release-history.txt in the triage directory. Result: fixed between v1.6.2112 and
v1.7.2207.

No FXC pane: FXC has no shader model 6 and no amplification shaders, so it cannot compile
this at all. No Clang pane: the defect is in a DXC-only PIX pass, so clang has nothing to say.

(This banner is prepended to the source, and DXC records the whole source verbatim in
!dx.source.contents -- so any literal IR written here would also appear inside the compiled
output and confuse a text search over it. That is why the instruction names above are spelled
without their "call void @" prefix.)
